messages.content:
You are writing for a bank's internal auditor, in UK English.
For each finding, write 2-3 plain sentences: what is wrong, why it matters, what to do.
Use ONLY the numbers given. Do not add, round, combine or calculate numbers.
Do not name customers. Return JSON: {"findings": {"<id>": "<text>", ...}}

{"CA1": "Strong red flag worth only 7 points: R07_split_money_orders. 7 pts, right 100.0% of the time (87-100%, n=25). 2 or more money orders paid in on one day, totalling £2,000-£2,499. When investigators reviewed customers this rule flagged, 100% were laundering, 10.4x the average, yet it adds only 7 of the 20 points needed for a case. Suggested fix: Raise R07_split_money_orders from 7 to about 20 points.", "BL1": "50 customers with no case look highly unusual. top 50 of 47,685 unflagged customers. These customers never reached the alarm level, but their behaviour is among the most unusual in the bank. Top reasons: 8270109607: money in from abroad (£) 403,572 (top 0.4% of customers); money in (£) 403,572 (top 0.4% of customers); most deposits in one day 2 (top 2% of customers) | 7494130236: money in from abroad (£) 510,361 (top 0.1% of customers); money in (£) 510,361 (top 0.1% of customers); high-risk-country transactions 16 (top 0.8% of customers) | 1000291638: money in from abroad (£) 312,127 (top 0.8% of customers); money in (£) 312,127 (top 1% of customers); share of money via high-risk countries 86% (top 3% of customers) Suggested fix: Send these customers for manual review, starting from rank 1.", "CV1": "Credit card payments (out) are only checked by a transaction count. only R06_velocity: £3,095,313,643. The only rule that can fire counts payments; it never looks at amounts, countries or who is being paid. Suggested fix: Add amount and counterparty rules for credit card payments (out).", "CV2": "Debit card payments (out) are only checked by a transaction count. only R06_velocity: £3,085,585,977. The only rule that can fire counts payments; it never looks at amounts, countries or who is being paid. Suggested fix: Add amount and counterparty rules for debit card payments (out)."}

reply: {"findings":{"CA1":"The rule R07_split_money_orders only contributes 7 points, even though it flags 2 or more money orders totalling £2,000‑£2,499 and was 100.0% correct in the sample of 25 cases. Because it adds only 7 of the 20 points needed for a case, it may miss high‑risk activity despite a 100% hit rate and a 10.4x increase over the average. Raise the rule weight from 7 to about 20 points so it can trigger a case on its own.","BL1":"Fifty unflagged customers appear in the top 50 of 47,685, showing unusually high inbound amounts such as £403,572 (top 0.4%) and £510,361 (top 0.1%). These patterns, including most deposits in one day of 2 (top 2%) and high‑risk‑country activity up to 86% (top 3%), suggest potential money‑laundering risk despite no alarm being raised. Send the customers for manual review, starting from rank 1.","CV1":"Credit card outbound payments are only screened by the R06_velocity rule, which counts transactions and currently covers £3,095,313,643. Because the rule ignores payment amounts, countries and counterparties, suspicious activity could go undetected. Add amount and counterparty rules for credit card outbound payments.","CV2":"Debit card outbound payments are only screened by the R06_velocity rule, which counts transactions and currently covers £3,085,585,977. Because the rule ignores payment amounts, countries and counterparties, suspicious activity could go undetected. Add amount and counterparty rules for debit card outbound payments."}}
